نُبُوحٌ (tropical:) The clamour, confused noise, or mixture of voices, of a tribe, (S,) or of a people, (K,) and the barkings of their dogs, (S, K,) and the cries of their other animals. (A.) ―
-b2- Subsequently put in the place of (tropical:) Multitude, and might, or power: (S:) and signifying (tropical:) a numerous assembly. (K.) El-Akhtal says, “إِنَّ العَرَارَةَ وَالنُّبُوحَ لِدَارِمٍ
”
[Verily strength, or eminence, or lordship, and multitude, and might, or power, belong to Dárim]. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
